2608.08182.title: Biologically Informed Representation Learning for Robust Cross-Center Generalization of MALDI-TOF Mass Spectrometry
2608.08182.paper_summary: Machine learning models for MALDI-TOF mass spectrometry have shown considerable promise for clinical microbiology tasks such as microbial identification and antimicrobial resistance prediction. However, their deployment across institutions remains limited by domain shift, as acquisition-specific variability often leads models to capture technical artifacts rather than transferable biological information. Existing representation learning approaches primarily address this problem through statistical domain alignment while largely overlooking the biological supervision naturally available in microbiology datasets. We introduce DALMA, a probabilistic representation learning framework that jointly models acquisition-specific variability and biological supervision to learn biologically structured latent representations. By combining domain-specific reconstruction with biologically guided representation learning, DALMA learns transferable representations that generalize across heterogeneous clinical centers without requiring institution-specific components at inference, enabling zero-shot deployment on previously unseen sites. We evaluate DALMA on a multi-center benchmark comprising seven datasets from three countries. DALMA consistently achieves state-of-the-art zero-shot microbial identification across two held-out clinical centers, while the learned representations also transfer effectively to antimicrobial resistance prediction. Furthermore, latent-space novelty estimation enables reliable selective prediction under previously unseen domain shifts. These results demonstrate that biologically informed representation learning provides an effective strategy for robust and transferable ML in clinical microbiology.
2608.08182.paper_summary_zh: 機器學習模型在MALDI-TOF質譜分析中對於臨床微生物學任務如微生物識別和抗微生物抗性預測顯示出相當大的潛力。<lb/>然而，它們在不同機構之間的應用仍然受到領域轉移的限制，因為特定於獲取的變異性往往導致模型捕捉到技術性伪影，而非可轉移的生物信息。<lb/>現有的表示學習方法主要通過統計領域對齊來解決這個問題，但在很大程度上忽視了微生物數據集中自然可用的生物監督。<lb/>我們介紹了DALMA，一種概率表示學習框架，該框架共同建模特定於獲取的變異性和生物監督，以學習生物結構化的潛在表示。<lb/>通過將特定於領域的重建與生物指導的表示學習相結合，DALMA學習可轉移的表示，這些表示在異質臨床中心之間具有良好的泛化能力，而在推斷時不需要特定於機構的組件，從而實現了在以前未見過的地點的零樣本部署。<lb/>我們在一個包含來自三個國家的七個數據集的多中心基準上評估了DALMA。<lb/>DALMA在兩個保留的臨床中心中始終實現了最先進的零樣本微生物識別，同時學習到的表示也有效地轉移到抗微生物抗性預測中。<lb/>此外，潛在空間的新穎性估計使得在以前未見的領域轉移下進行可靠的選擇性預測成為可能。<lb/>這些結果表明，生物信息驅動的表示學習為臨床微生物學中的穩健和可轉移的機器學習提供了一種有效的策略。
